_meta.role: Robotics Software Engineer - Guidance, Navigation and Control

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), graduating May 2026, focused on robotics control, perception, and real-time embedded systems. Built ROS2-based manipulation pipelines using MoveIt and DH-parameter kinematics, and an autonomous driving stack in CARLA combining YOLO and UFLD perception with an adaptive lane-following and waypoint control loop. Comfortable across the full sensor-to-deployment path in C++ and Python, from STM32 and Jetson controllers to closed-loop servo and motor control.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team, owning mechanical design and PCB fabrication in EAGLE; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition system integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi over Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into real-time control commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Architected a full metal surface inspection pipeline combining custom image stitching and ZoeDepth monocular depth estimation, reaching plus or minus 8% error on 3D surface reconstruction.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built automated CARLA data generation pipelines producing roughly 5,000 YOLO and 3,000 UFLD training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n and fine-tuned UFLD to feed an adaptive control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback.
Validated in Town02 with 30 vehicles and 10 pedestrians, achieving zero collisions and correct traffic-light compliance across multiple laps.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and forward kinematic chains for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B, validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e; AL5B repeatability measured under 2mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects in real time, sending control commands to an STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands, FreeRTOS task coordination, and closed-loop VL53L0X ToF sensing for distance feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system on a Flask-SocketIO edge server and Jetson plus Arduino controller, using TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on an Arduino in C++, driving five servos to achieve 100% pick reliability across 10 trials.
